Fix the pipe. Keep the driveway.

Minimal-digging sewer repair that saves your yard and driveway. Flip the switch to see what the same repair looks like both ways.

Repair method
Call (844) 212-9186

Two ways to do it without a trench

Pipe lining

How it works

  1. We clean the old pipe so the liner can stick to it.
  2. A soft liner soaked in resin is pulled into the pipe.
  3. It's pressed against the walls and left to harden into a new pipe inside the old one.

A good fit when

The pipe is cracked, worn or leaking at the joints, but still runs in a straight line.

Not a good fit when

The pipe has sagged, collapsed or sits out of line. A liner follows the old pipe, so it can't fix the shape. It also makes the inside slightly narrower.

Pipe bursting

How it works

  1. We dig a small hole at each end of the line.
  2. A bursting head is pulled through the old pipe, breaking it outward into the soil.
  3. A new pipe is pulled in right behind it.

A good fit when

The old pipe is badly damaged, collapsed or too far gone to line.

Not a good fit when

Other utilities run close by, or the soil won't allow it. We locate those first, and we'll tell you if bursting isn't safe.

Digging or not digging

TopicDigging a trenchTrenchless
What gets dugA trench along the whole pipeUsually two small access holes
Driveway, garden, treesCut through, then put back afterwardMostly left alone
Best forPipe that is badly sagging or out of lineCracked, worn, root-damaged or some collapsed pipe
Good to knowThe price includes putting the yard backNot every pipe qualifies. The camera decides.

How a trenchless job goes

camera first, always

  1. 1

    Camera first

    We look inside the pipe to see whether trenchless will work at all.

  2. 2

    Clean the line

    Roots and buildup come out so the repair has a clean surface.

  3. 3

    Open two small holes

    One near the house and one near the street, or wherever the pipe allows.

  4. 4

    Lining or bursting

    We use the method that suits your pipe.

  5. 5

    Camera again

    We check the new pipe from the inside before we close up.

  6. 6

    Tidy up

    Holes get filled and the area is left clean.

Straight answers

Is trenchless always an option?

No. If the pipe has sagged badly or collapsed in a way that can't be worked around, digging is the honest answer. We'll say so.

Is it cheaper?

Not always. The repair itself can cost more than digging, but you skip paying to rebuild the driveway, patio or garden. If both options work, we quote both.

Will it last?

A properly installed liner or new pipe is meant to last for decades. We'll tell you what to expect for your specific pipe and how our work is done to code.

Want to keep your yard?

Let's see if your pipe qualifies.

We start with a camera inspection, then tell you honestly whether trenchless will work.
